question: In the MUTCD treatment of changeable message signs, what is a unit of information and how many words should it contain at most?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In the MUTCD's treatment of changeable message signs, a unit of information is a single answer to a single question that a driver can use to make a decision (e.g., "What happened?" → "MAJOR CRASH"). As Guidance (recommended practice), a unit of information should not be more than four words, and the total number of units in a message governs its maximum length. Guidance (recommended): - "A unit of information, which is a single answer to a single question that a driver can use to make a decision, should not be more than four words." The maximum message length should be dictated by the number of units of information plus the size of the CMS. - Related principles: no more than three units of information should be displayed in a message phase; no more than four units in a message when traffic operating speeds are 35 mph or more; no more than five units when speeds are less than 35 mph; and only one unit of information should appear on each line of the CMS. Options (permitted): - A unit of information consisting of more than one word may be displayed on more than one line, and an additional downstream CMS may be used so the entire message can be read twice. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 2L-2 illustrates four units of information as question/answer pairs (What happened? → MAJOR CRASH; Where? → AT EXIT 12; Who is the advisory for? → drivers heading TO NEW YORK; What is advised? → USE ROUTE 46), and shows how they can be arranged into a two-phase message ("MAJOR CRASH / AT EXIT 12" and "USE ROUTE 46 / TO NEW YORK"). Citations: - Section 2L.05 Guidance §1 (p.514) - Section 2L.05 Guidance §7 (p.516) - Section 2L.05 Option §9 (p.516) - Section 2L.05 Support §2 (p.515) - Section 2L.05 Support §3 (p.515) - Table 2L-2 (p.515)
gold_answer: A unit of information is one answer to one question that a driver can use to make a decision. It should contain no more than four words; total message length should be governed by the number of information units and the size of the CMS.
